text:
maria.chen: Heads-up — during a customer private deployment smoke test we saw the keystore sidecar making outbound POSTs to telemetry.example.com shortly after key unwrap. Not sure if this is expected (metrics ping) or a netpol gap. Anyone on netpol/keystore handshake history?
aj: Not normal. Sidecar should only call our local kms-proxy or HSM. Can you paste the netpol for the keystore namespace?
maria.chen: Pasting minimal policy we applied: ```yaml apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1 kind: NetworkPolicy metadata: name: keystore-egress namespace: keystore spec: podSelector: matchLabels: app: keystore policyTypes: - Egress egress: - to: - podSelector: matchLabels: role: kms-proxy ports: - protocol: TCP port: 443 ``` It allows egress to `kms-proxy` but the sidecar is still hitting external host.
irene: Two quick possibilities: 1) DNS egress allowed via CNI hostNetwork path, or 2) the sidecar uses an init container to seed telemetry and that runs before netpol enforcement.
sam: Also check the pod's serviceAccount and projected tokens — if the sidecar spawns a short-lived job with a different SA that has broader egress, it could explain it.
aj: Run `kubectl get pods -n keystore -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name}{"\t"}{.spec.serviceAccountName}{"\n"}{end}'` and confirm SA mapping.
maria.chen: SA mapping looks correct — `keystore-sa` on all pods. I grabbed iptables nat rules on the node; nothing unusual. The external host is a CDN we use for telemetry, but we thought customer deployments block any non-proxied egress.
ops-bot: Incident note created: #INC-2026-keystore-egress (assigned to irene).
irene: Can you also paste the keystore sidecar args? Maybe `--telemetry-endpoint` is set via env from the ConfigMap and customer override slipped in.
maria.chen: ConfigMap shows `TELEMETRY_ENDPOINT: https://telemetry.example.com/collect`. Customer overlay should have replaced it with `null`; looks like overlay merge didn't run. Might be a packaging bug.
sam: Two follow-ups: 1) tighten netpol to block DNS egress except to kube-dns; 2) enforce egress via a transparent proxy (squid) and require TLS interception certificate pinned to internal CA so external host wouldn't validate.
aj: For immediate mitigation, apply this egress-deny default to keystore namespace: ```yaml apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1 kind: NetworkPolicy metadata: name: deny-egress-default namespace: keystore spec: podSelector: {} policyTypes: - Egress egress: [] ``` That should block non-allowed egress while we patch the overlay.
maria.chen: Applying now to staging. Will report if external traffic stops.
sec-bot: Reminder: update audit retention for private deploys to include sidecar logs and KMS-proxy transcripts. Default is 30d; ops requested 90d for this customer.
irene: Forensics note — we need KMS request IDs correlated with sidecar process IDs. Ensure the kms-proxy adds `X-Request-ID` header and we ship that to SIEM. Also enable structured JSON logging in keystore sidecar for easier parsing.
sam: One more; if the customer uses an HSM with on-prem control, confirm that our keystore proxy performs attestation handshakes only over mTLS to the attestation service and never falls back to plaintext. Add a config check in preflight.
aj: I'll open a quick PR with the overlay validation step and preflight check for `TELEMETRY_ENDPOINT == null` for private deploys. Tagging @irene for review.
maria.chen: Staging mitigation worked — no outbound to telemetry.example.com after deny policy applied. Good catch.
irene: Let's schedule a 30m postmortem and update the Private Deploy hardening checklist: - overlay merge validation step - deny-by-default netpol for sensitive namespaces - enforce transparent egress proxy in customer prod - audit log retention 90d - KMS-proxy X-Request-ID header - preflight HSM attestation check
sam: I'll take the checklist PR.
aj: PR opened: https://git.redwood/infra/keystore-overlay/patches/12 (wip).
maria.chen: Thanks all. Follow-up: can we add a short runbook entry to incident response playbook for "keystore unexpected egress" with quick mitigation steps? cc @ops-bot
ops-bot: Runbook item created at https://redwood.internal/runbooks/keystore-egress.
sec-bot: Closing note: mark this as low-sev since no keys were exfiltrated and HSM attestation validated. Keep monitoring. :thumbsup:
